newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to hike fresh milk prices in Q4 - Canilec.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to hike fresh milk prices in Q4 - Canilec.

text.p: Pasteurised milk prices will rise 5 percent in the final quarter of 1997, the outgoing chairman of the National Milk Industry Chamber (Canilec) said Thursday.

Luis Miguel Hernandez told a media conference that the fourth quarter increase will take the prices of 1 liter of milk to 4.20 pesos and added that government plans were to free up price controls on milk next year.
Milk alongside corn pancakes tortillas are the only two basic food products with prices set by the government. Controls on other basics have been lifted in recent years

Hernandez said he did not believe free milk prices to the supply and demand of the market would not bring an exaggerated rise in prices. He explain that in the northern border areas milk prices are now not controlled and prices have not gone through the roof.
Mexico's move to lift controls on milk aims to boost investment in the dairy sector. In 1996, Mexico imported around 17 percent of its milk -- a staggering 4.5 million liters of milk.
Mexico is the world's largest milk powder importer. Hernandez said last year milk powder imports reached 46,670 tonnes.
